name: ProcessPlatform

test_list.description: Relative program paths and unknown opaque process handles are rejected before an OS PID lookup can occur.
Explicit secret-like environment keys and duplicate case-normalized names are denied.
A real worker tree stops its grandchild through the OS process group or Job Object and receives only its explicit non-secret environment.
Dropping the final platform owner force-stops the retained tree, including a grandchild.
The measured available-memory ratio maps at 5%, 6%, 15%, and 16% to Critical, Elevated, Elevated, and Normal; zero total memory is an error.
Windows-only: forcibly terminate the owner process, bypassing Rust Drop, and observe the grandchild exit through JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE.

inputs.name: spawn_spec
inputs.description: Absolute executable path, argument vector, optional working directory, and complete explicit environment allowlist. Secret-like keys are rejected and inherited host environment is cleared.

inputs.name: process_tree
inputs.description: Root PID paired with an opaque adapter-owned live handle. Runtime signals resolve the retained group or Job Object and never re-resolve a PID.

output_description: A retained native process tree with nonblocking exit observation, graceful stop followed by force stop, and synchronous force-stop for Drop guards.
